title: Algebraicity of a stack with a representable fppf algebraic-space cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal Y$ be a stack in groupoids on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Thus isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and covering descent data for objects are effective. Let $A$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid, and let $f:A\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of fibred groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $A\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ is equivalent to an algebraic space $A_y$ over $T$. Suppose every projection $A_y\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and surjective, meaning that every field-valued point of $T$ lifts after a field extension. Then $\mathcal Y$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. No representability hypothesis on the diagonal of $\mathcal Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06DC (theorem-bootstrap), with the source stack represented by the algebraic space A.

proof.text: First derive the diagonal, following Tag 05XW. For $y_1,y_2\in\mathcal Y(T)$ let $I=\operatorname{Isom}_T(y_1,y_2)$, an fppf sheaf by hypothesis. Put $A_i=A\times_{\mathcal Y,y_i}T$ and $B=A\times_ST$. The $A_i$ are algebraic spaces by the assumption on $f$; $B$ and $P=A_1\times_BA_2$ are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], using [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to regard these as spaces over $T$. A section of $P$ consists of a common $(a,t)$ and isomorphisms $\alpha_i:f(a)\simeq y_i|_t$. Send it to $\alpha_2\alpha_1^{-1}\in I$. For every scheme $Z\to T$ and $\phi\in I(Z)$, $P\times_IZ\simeq A_1\times_TZ$: choose $\alpha_1$, then necessarily $\alpha_2=\phi\alpha_1$. This is natural, with inverse forgetting $\alpha_2$. The resulting projection is surjective flat locally finitely presented by the singleton base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. Thus [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] makes $I$ an algebraic space. These are exactly the scheme pullbacks of the diagonal, so the diagonal is representable; no diagonal hypothesis has been used.

For every $d\geq1$ form $H_d=\mathcal H_d(f)$ and $L_d=\mathcal L_d(f)$ using [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. By [lem-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-algebraic], $H_d$ is algebraic: the source is the given space $A$, and all its scheme fibres have precisely the assumed surjective flat locally finitely presented projections. By [lem-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-lci-open] the inclusion $L_d\to H_d$ has open scheme pullbacks. Apply [lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp] to obtain that $L_d$ is algebraic. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $q_d:V_d\to L_d$ as in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Let $g_d:V_d\to\mathcal Y$ forget the finite family. Step 1 and [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] show that every $g_d$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

The inclusion $L_d\to H_d$ has locally finitely presented scheme pullbacks: an open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence locally finitely presented by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The atlas $q_d$ also has locally finitely presented space pullbacks, because its smooth etale scheme charts are locally finitely presented by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] identifies the chart and space properties. Therefore [lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test] gives relative object descent for each of these two maps. Given an affine directed limit $T=\lim T_i$, $v\in V_d(T)$, and an identification $g_d(v)\simeq y_i|_T$, first descend its $H_d$ object over $y_i$ by [lem-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-limit-descent]. Next descend its $L_d$ object over this $H_d$ object using the inclusion, and finally descend $v$ over that $L_d$ object using $q_d$. At each stage retain the specified comparison isomorphism; their composites identify $g_d(v_j)$ with $y_i|_{T_j}$. This is the relative object-descent property for $g_d$. Apply the converse of [lem-sfb-representable-lfp-object-limit-test] to this representable map: all $V_d\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T$ are locally of finite presentation.

The map $g_d$ has etale-local compatible square-zero object lifts. Given affine $T_0\hookrightarrow T'$, $v_0\in V_d(T_0)$, $y'\in\mathcal Y(T')$ and $g_d(v_0)\simeq y'|_{T_0}$, apply [lem-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-lci-lift] to $q_d(v_0)$. Obtain $l'\in L_d(T')$ and its compatible identification with $y'$. The smooth space $E=V_d\times_{L_d,l'}T'$ has the specified $T_0$-point. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $C\to E$. Its pullback $C_0\to T_0$ along this point is a surjective etale scheme cover by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site] it lifts to an etale cover $C'\to T'$. Replace $C'$ by affine open pieces $B'_a$, with $B_{a0}=B'_a\times_{T'}T_0$. The map $C\to T'$ is smooth by the chart definition, so [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] extends each $B_{a0}\to C$ to $B'_a\to C$ over $T'$. Projection through $E$ gives $v'_a:B'_a\to V_d$ and compatible isomorphisms $g_d(v'_a)\simeq y'|_{B'_a}$ restricting to the specified data on $B_{a0}$. The $B'_a$ cover $T'$; the fibre-product data retain the original comparison isomorphism.

Fix $T\to\mathcal Y$ and $Z_d=V_d\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, an algebraic space locally finitely presented over $T$ by steps 2--3. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $W\to Z_d$. By [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], $W\to T$ is locally finitely presented. Given affine $B_0\hookrightarrow B'$ over $T$ and $B_0\to W$, step 4 gives an affine etale cover $B'_a\to B'$ and maps $B'_a\to Z_d$ extending its composite. The pullback $D_a=W\times_{Z_d}B'_a$ is a scheme etale over $B'_a$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with the prescribed section over $B_{a0}$. Its map to $B'_a$ is flat and unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] extends this section to $B'_a\to D_a$, giving etale-local lifts to $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-local-infinitesimal-lifts-smooth] to the scheme map $W\to T$ to obtain smoothness. The property smooth is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], so [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] with target chart $T\to T$ makes $Z_d\to T$ smooth.

For a field-valued object $y\in\mathcal Y(k)$, the given fibre $A_y$ is nonempty and locally finitely presented over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-lci-field] to obtain $Z\to A_y$ with $Z/k$ finite locally free of some positive degree $d$, unramified and lci. Its map to $A_y$ is exactly a pair $(x,\alpha:y|_Z\simeq f(x))$ by the definition of the 2-fibre product, hence gives $l\in L_d(k)$ by [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. The surjectivity of $q_d$ gives, after a field extension $k\subseteq K$, a $K$-point of $V_d$ mapping isomorphically to $l|_K$. Consequently the family $(g_d)_{d\geq1}$ is jointly surjective on field-valued objects.

Form the countable scheme coproduct $V=\coprod_{d\geq1}V_d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The objects $g_d$ glue to a map $g:V\to\mathcal Y$ by stack descent on its disjoint open cover. The diagonal from step 1 and [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] make $g$ representable. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, its pullback is the coproduct of the $Z_d$ of step 5: on test schemes this is the decomposition into inverse images of the open summands of $V$. Each etale scheme chart of this pullback decomposes into open pieces mapping to the $Z_d$, so its composite to $T$ is smooth by step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. Thus $g$ is smooth. Step 6 makes $g$ surjective. Finally the fppf stack $\mathcal Y$ is an etale stack since etale coverings are fppf by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. Together with step 1 and the smooth surjective scheme atlas $g$, these are precisely [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack].

lean.statement: theorem fppf_stack_algebraicity_bootstrap {S : Scheme.{u}} (Y : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hstack : IsFppfModuliStack Y) (A : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli A.obj.obj) Y) (hcover : ∀ (T : Over S) (y : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) Y), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange f T y Z p ∧ (∀ (U : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Z.obj.obj), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale b → Flat (yoneda.preimage (b ≫ p)).left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (yoneda.preimage (b ≫ p)).left) ∧ SpaceMapIsSurjective Z T p) : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Y
